titleEn: Lighting Renovation in Vancouver: Costs, Types, and Permit Requirements
titleZh: 溫哥華照明裝修：費用、類型與許可證要求
contentEn:
Vancouver homeowners often overlook lighting during a renovation. New fixtures, recessed cans, and LED upgrades transform how a home looks and functions — and in British Columbia, electrical work requires a permit regardless of whether you are doing a full renovation or a targeted upgrade. This guide covers the types of lighting renovations available in Vancouver, what each costs based on 2025–2026 contract data, and what the permit process involves.

What Is a Lighting Renovation in Vancouver?

A lighting renovation in Vancouver or Metro Vancouver covers any electrical lighting work done as part of a larger home renovation project. This includes new fixture installation, electrical rough-in for recessed cans, panel upgrades to support additional circuits, and LED retrofits. Lighting work is often done alongside a kitchen or bathroom renovation but can also be scoped as a standalone project.

Reno Stars' 2025–2026 project data shows lighting upgrades are most commonly combined with kitchen renovations (recessed under-cabinet LED strips, pendant fixtures over islands, updated recessed ceiling cans) and bathroom renovations (vanity lighting, exhaust fan with light combos, heated flooring controls).

How Much Does a Lighting Renovation Cost in Vancouver?

Based on 2025–2026 Reno Stars contracts across Metro Vancouver, lighting renovation costs break down as follows:

  • Recessed can lights (6-inch standard): $150–$350 per fixture including labour and materials, depending on whether rough-in wiring exists
  • LED under-cabinet strip lighting: $200–$600 per kitchen run, typically installed during a kitchen renovation
  • Pendant fixture installation: $100–$250 per fixture for labour, plus the cost of the fixture itself
  • Electrical panel upgrade to support additional circuits: $3,000–$7,500 depending on amperage and BC Electrical Code requirements
  • Full lighting rough-in for new buildout or basement suite: $1,500–$4,000 depending on number of circuits and fixtures
  • Smart lighting control integration (Wi-Fi or Lutron-style switches): $200–$600 per room, switch equipment and hub included

Do Lighting Renovations Need a Permit in BC?

Yes. In British Columbia, any lighting work that involves altering wires — adding, moving, or replacing fixtures — requires an electrical permit from Technical Safety BC. This applies in the City of Vancouver, Metro Vancouver, and across BC. Simple fixture swaps where you are replacing a like-for-like fitting in the same location (swapping one pendant for another) do not require a permit. New recessed can installation, new circuit runs, panel upgrades, and any work in wet areas (bathrooms, kitchens) all require a permit.

A licensed electrical contractor applies for the permit. Reno Stars uses electrical sub-contractors who handle all permit applications and arrange BC electrical inspections as part of the project.

LED vs Recessed: Which Lighting Upgrade Gives Vancouver Homeowners the Best Return?

For Vancouver homeowners considering a renovation investment, LED retrofit upgrades and recessed can installation consistently offer the best return on resale value and energy efficiency. LED fixtures use approximately 75 percent less energy than equivalent incandescent bulbs and last 25 times longer. In a kitchen renovation, swapping fluorescent under-cabinet lighting for an LED strip typically costs $300–$600 and reduces that area's lighting energy draw by approximately 40 watts.

Recessed cans add perceived ceiling height and work well in Vancouver's modern open-concept homes. IC-rated airtight 6-inch recessed cans with LED bulbs that meet BC Building Code cost $150–$250 per unit installed.

How to Plan a Lighting Renovation in Your Vancouver Home

Before booking a contractor, Vancouver homeowners should plan which rooms need updated lighting, which fixtures are fixed (recessed cans, vanity strips) and which are decorative (pendants, table lamps). This distinction determines whether a permit is required. Note your electrical panel capacity — a 100-amp panel may not have space for new 15-amp or 20-amp circuits required for additional lighting zones. If you are considering adding a basement suite or secondary suite as part of your renovation, a panel upgrade is almost certainly required, typically adding $3,000–$7,500 to project cost.

Frequently Asked Questions About Lighting Renovations in Vancouver

How much does recessed can lighting cost to install in Vancouver?

IC-rated airtight 6-inch recessed cans in Metro Vancouver cost $150–$350 per unit installed. The range depends on whether rough-in wiring is already in place (lower cost) or a new circuit must be run from the panel (higher cost). A typical kitchen with six recessed cans plus under-cabinet LED strips — including materials, labour, permits, and inspection — runs $1,200–$2,400 total.

Do lighting renovations require an electrical permit in BC?

Yes. Any electrical work in BC that involves adding, moving, or altering lighting wiring requires an electrical permit from Technical Safety BC. A licensed electrical contractor applies for the permit and schedules required inspections. Performing electrical work without a permit can result in fines and mandatory re-inspection. Reno Stars' electrical sub-contractors handle all permit applications and inspections for lighting projects.

What is the average cost of an electrical panel upgrade in Vancouver?

Upgrading an electrical panel to 200 amps in Vancouver or Metro Vancouver costs $3,000–$7,500. The range reflects amperage requirements, whether the service entry cable also needs replacement, and BC Electrical Code compliance work. A panel upgrade is typically required when adding a basement suite, hot tub, EV charger, or multiple new lighting circuits.

Are LED recessed cans better than surface-mount fixtures for Vancouver homes?

LED recessed cans generally provide better visual appeal and resale value in Vancouver's contemporary open-concept homes than surface-mount fixtures. IC-rated airtight recessed cans prevent air leakage — important for BC's energy efficiency standards — and produce cleaner ceiling lines. Surface-mount fixtures are appropriate where ceiling height is limited or where the electrical box is surface-run.

Can Reno Stars handle a lighting renovation alongside a full kitchen remodel?

Yes. Reno Stars routinely coordinates lighting upgrades as part of full kitchen, bathroom, and whole-home renovations in Vancouver, Richmond, Burnaby, Coquitlam, and West Vancouver. All electrical work is performed by licensed sub-contractors, permits are arranged, and inspections are completed before project sign-off.

contentZh:
照明裝修是溫哥華業主在裝修時常忽略的環節。新燈具、嵌入式筒燈和LED升級不僅改變家居外觀和功能，也在 BC 省必須根據電氣條例申請許可。本文涵蓋溫哥華照明裝修的類型、2025-2026 年實際工程造價數據，以及許可證流程。

什麼是溫哥華照明裝修？

溫哥華或大溫哥華都會區的照明裝修涵蓋房屋裝修中進行的任何電氣照明工程，包括新燈具安裝、嵌入式筒燈電氣布線、面板升級以支持額外電路，以及 LED 改造。照明工程通常與廚房或浴室裝修同時進行，也可作為獨立項目。

根據 Reno Stars 2025-2026 年工程數據，照明升級最常與廚房裝修（嵌入式 LED 燈帶、島台上方的吊燈、更新天花板嵌入式筒燈）和浴室裝修（洗手台照明、排氣扇連燈、發熱地板溫控器）相結合。

溫哥華照明裝修費用是多少？

根據大溫哥華 2025-2026 年 Reno Stars 已簽訂合同數據，照明裝修費用如下：

  • 嵌入式筒燈（6 英寸標準）：每個 $150–$350，包括人工和材料，視乎是否已有布線
  • 櫥櫃下方 LED 燈帶：每廚房段 $200–$600，通常在廚房裝修時一併安裝
  • 吊燈安裝：每個 $100–$250 人工費，另有燈具本身費用
  • 電氣面板升級以支持額外電路：$3,000–$7,500，視乎安培容量和 BC 電氣條例要求
  • 新建區域或地下室套間的照明布線：$1,500–$4,000，視乎電路數量和燈具數量
  • 智能照明控制集成（Wi-Fi 或 Lutron 風格開關）：每房間 $200–$600，包括開關設備和集線器

計劃進行廚房、浴室、全屋或商業裝修？聯繫 Reno Stars 獲取免費、無義務報價。

BC 省照明工程是否需要許可證？

需要。在卑詩省，任何涉及電線改動的照明工程——包括添加、移動或更換燈具——都需要向 Technical Safety BC 申請電氣許可證。這適用於溫哥華市，大溫哥華都會區及整個 BC 省。不涉及電線改動的簡單燈具更換（在相同位置將吊燈換為另一吊燈）無需許可證。嵌入式筒燈安裝、新電路鋪設、面板升級以及任何潮濕區域（浴室、廚房）的工程均必須申請許可證。

持牌電氣承包商負責申請許可證。Reno Stars 使用的電氣分包商負責辦理所有許可證申請並安排 BC 電氣檢驗。

LED 與嵌入式：哪種照明升級在溫哥華回報最高？

對於考慮裝修投資的溫哥華業主，LED 改造升級和嵌入式筒燈安裝在轉售和能源效益方面始終提供最佳回報。LED 燈具比同等白熾燈節省約 75% 能源，壽命長 25 倍。在廚房裝修中，將螢光燈管櫃下照明換為 LED 燈帶通常費用為 $300–$600，該區域照明能耗降低約 40 瓦。

嵌入式筒燈可增加空間感，特別適合溫哥華的現代開放式住宅。符合 BC 建築條例的 6 英寸 IC 等級氣密嵌入式筒燈（LED 燈泡）每個 $150–$250 安裝費。

如何規劃溫哥華住宅的照明裝修？

在預訂承包商之前，溫哥華業主應先規劃哪些房間需要更新照明，哪些燈具是固定的（嵌入式筒燈、洗手台燈帶），哪些是裝飾性的（吊燈、枱燈）。這一區分決定是否需要許可證。記錄您配電箱的容量——100 安培的面板可能沒有空間容納新照明區域所需的 15 安培或 20 安培電路。如果考慮在裝修中興建地下室套間或第二套間，幾乎必然需要進行面板升級，通常增加 $3,000–$7,500 的項目成本。

  • Delta 廚房裝修 — LED 嵌入式和櫃下照明
  • 高貴林公寓廚房裝修
  • 列治文白色鄉村風廚房裝修

溫哥華照明裝修常見問題

溫哥華安裝嵌入式筒燈多少錢？

大溫哥華地區符合 IC 等級的 6 英寸氣密嵌入式筒燈每個 $150–$350 安裝費。費用範圍取決於是否已有布線（費用較低）或需要從配電箱鋪設新電路（費用較高）。一般廚房 6 個嵌入式筒燈加櫃下 LED 燈帶，全套（包括材料、人工、許可證和檢驗）費用為 $1,200–$2,400。

BC 照明工程需要許可證嗎？

需要。卑詩省任何涉及添加、移動或改動照明電線的電氣工程都需要向 Technical Safety BC 申請電氣許可證。持牌電氣承包商負責申請許可證並安排所需檢驗，未經許可進行電氣工程可能面臨罰款和強制重新檢驗。Reno Stars 使用的電氣分包商負責辦理照明工程的所有許可證申請和檢驗。

溫哥華電氣面板升級平均費用是多少？

溫哥華或大溫哥華將電氣面板升級至 200 安培費用為 $3,000–$7,500。範圍取決於安培容量需求、入戶電纜是否需要更換，以及 BC 電氣條例合規工作。增設地下室套間、熱水浴缸、電動車充電樁或多個新照明電路時，通常需要進行面板升級。

LED 嵌入式筒燈比表面安裝燈具更適合溫哥華住宅嗎？

LED 嵌入式筒燈通常比表面安裝燈具更能提升溫哥華當代開放式住宅的視覺效果和轉售價值。IC 等級氣密嵌入式筒燈防止空氣滲漏——對 BC 省能源效益標準非常重要——並產生更乾淨的天花板線條。表面安裝燈具適用於天花板高度有限或需要表面布線的情況。

Reno Stars 能在廚房改造的同時處理照明裝修嗎？

能。Reno Stars 定期在大溫哥華、列治文、本拿比、高貴林和西溫哥華的廚房、浴室和全屋裝修中協調照明升級。所有電氣工程均由持牌分包商完成，許可證由他們代為申請，工程驗收前完成所有檢驗。
